name: Obertilliach
kurzbeschreibung: Sunny mountain village in the upper Gailtal with the Biathlon-Zentrum and the Naturpark.
beschreibung:
Overview

Obertilliach is situated in the scenic high valley of the Tyrolean Gail Valley in the East Tyrolean district of Lienz, nestled between the Lienz Dolomites to the north and the Carnic Ridge to the south at an altitude of 1,450 metres. This heritage-rich mountain municipality has around 660 residents and spans 65 square kilometres bordering Carinthia and Italy. As an official member of the prestigious Mountaineering Villages initiative, Obertilliach is wholeheartedly committed to preserving its pristine alpine nature and centuries-old farming heritage. The architectural crown of the village is its protected historic centre: sun-blackened timber houses clustered tightly together form one of the best-preserved nucleated wooden villages in the entire Alpine region. Obertilliach is also renowned as the home of Austria's last traditional night watchman, who still patrols the historic lanes at night with a halberd, lantern, and traditional chant.

History

The high valley was first documented in written records in 1075 under the name Tillach. For centuries, the inhabitants lived in relative isolation, sustained by alpine farming and forestry under severe high-mountain conditions. Due to the constant risk of catastrophic fire in such a tightly packed wooden settlement, a strict night watchman ordinance was established in the 17th century; this unbroken tradition endures to this day, enchanting visitors from across the globe. The outstanding religious monument is the Baroque Parish Church of St. Ulrich, erected between 1762 and 1764 to designs by the famed Tyrolean church architect Franz de Paula Penz, featuring splendid ceiling frescoes by Anton Zoller. In 2015, the historic wooden ensemble earned global fame when it served as a primary filming location for the James Bond blockbuster Spectre starring Daniel Craig.

Getting There

Reaching Obertilliach takes travellers through the majestic mountain sceneries of East Tyrol and Carinthia. By car, journey from Lienz along the Drau Valley Road B100 to Tassenbach in the Puster Valley, turning onto the Gailtal Road B111 over the Kartitscher Sattel pass directly into Obertilliach in about 35 minutes. From Carinthia, the B111 leads westward from Hermagor and Kötschach-Mauthen through the Lesach Valley. Rail travellers take the Puster Valley Railway to Tassenbach or Sillian stations. From there, frequent regional buses operated by Verkehrsverbund Tirol (VVT) run directly into Obertilliach village centre and to the Biathlon Centre. In the winter season, complimentary local ski buses connect all points of interest throughout the valley.

Tips

The sporting flagship of the village is the Biathlon Centre East Tyrol, a world-class training and competition facility where Olympic legend Ole Einar Bjørndalen lived and trained; during winter, more than 60 kilometres of meticulously groomed cross-country trails span the border region. Skiers and hikers head to the family-friendly Golzentipp ski area: the modern 10-seater Golzentippbahn gondola departs directly from the village centre up to 2,050 metres, granting access to sunny slopes and magnificent views of the Carnic Peace Trail. An evening tour through the historic village alleys following the night watchman is an unforgettable cultural highlight. In addition, the Carriage and Local Heritage Museum at the Lugger-Stadel displays over 50 historic horse carriages and antique farming equipment.
